answer: Randomized Vault Slot Assignment. Each registration epoch seeds a public beacon whose value is unknown until round close; agents draw from a vault address space with the beacon, so attacker addresses cannot be positioned ahead of time to cluster adjacent or batch-verify efficiently. Registration succeeds only if the drawn slot clears a threshold tied to verified work. An attacker cannot precompute favorable slots, so each extra identity costs a fresh full registration cycle, and idle addresses decay into umber inactivity.
